questions.question: Why do modern AI engineers prefer an end-to-end pipeline instead of writing all AI math from scratch?
options: Because the math is impossible to use
Because the pipeline lets them gather data, process it, run it through a pre-trained model, and return results efficiently
Because pre-trained models cannot be downloaded
Because AI apps do not need data

questions.question: Which platform is described as the central ecosystem used by the AI industry for building applied AI systems?
What are the three main pillars of the HuggingFace ecosystem mentioned in the chapter?
options: Models, datasets, and the Transformers library

questions.question: Which pillar of HuggingFace is most directly described as a package of Python code that connects models and datasets?
What is the best description of the Model Hub?
options: A library of training labels only
A massive library of pre-trained open-source AI models
A place where only raw text is stored

questions.question: What is the role of the Datasets Hub in the HuggingFace ecosystem?
options: It stores the final predictions of models
It provides text, image, and audio data used to train models
It converts output back into English
It ranks model answers using humans

questions.question: Why is the HuggingFace Transformers library especially important for AI engineers?
options: It lets engineers connect models and datasets with only a few lines of code
It removes the need for any data pipeline
It replaces tokenization with manual work

questions.question: What does ETL stand for in the data pipeline described in the chapter?
Which step in ETL is responsible for gathering messy raw material such as TikTok transcripts and Instagram captions?
Why is the Extract step in the chapter described as messy?
options: Because the data is already perfectly cleaned
Because it may contain typos, emojis, and broken links
Because it can only include numbers
Because it deletes all useful information

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Transform step in ETL?
options: To make raw data more useful by cleaning and translating it into numbers
To train the model with rewards and punishments
To send the answer directly to the screen

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically mentioned as part of the Transform step?
options: Removing broken links and weird computer code
Deleting all punctuation from the final output
Ranking answers from best to worst

questions.question: What does the Load step do in the ETL pipeline?
options: Sends cleaned numbers into the GPU so the model can learn
Deletes bad data from the internet

questions.question: In the chapter, cleaned numbers that are loaded into the model are also called:
Why must an AI pipeline use the exact tokenizer designed for a specific model?
options: Because every model shares the same dictionary
Because using the wrong dictionary would make the AI output gibberish
Because tokenizers only work with images
Because tokenizers replace the model itself

questions.question: What is a vocabulary in the context of tokenization?
options: A unique dictionary for a specific LLM

questions.question: In one model, the word 'Youth' may have a different token ID than in another model because:
options: The prompt is always the same
Token IDs are random and never model-specific

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of encoding in tokenization?
options: Turning a prompt into a list of integers
Turning integers back into English text

questions.question: What is the purpose of an attention mask?
options: To tell the AI which tokens are real and which are padding

questions.question: Which option best describes decoding?
options: Translating model output numbers back into readable English
Removing broken links from raw data

questions.question: In an end-to-end inference pipeline, what happens first after the user asks a question?
options: The model immediately writes the answer
The text is extracted and transformed by the tokenizer
The output is judged by humans
The reward model gives a penalty

questions.question: What is inference in simple technical terms?
options: Asking the AI a question and getting an answer
Loading raw links into the GPU

questions.question: What role does the pre-trained model play in the pipeline?
options: It processes the cleaned numerical input and predicts output numbers
It stores only the raw dataset
It serves as the human judge

questions.question: Which stage directly connects the model's numerical output to the visible final answer on screen?
What does mastering the pipeline allow an engineer to do?
options: Replace all datasets with manual rules

questions.question: During pre-training, what is the AI mainly taught to do?
options: Predict the next word by learning the basic rules of human language
Write only one specific type of email
Learn how to run a GPU

questions.question: What best describes a pre-trained model in the chapter's analogy?
options: A college graduate with general knowledge but no specific job training
A robot that can only do one task

questions.question: Fine-tuning is most accurately described as:
options: Teaching the AI general English from the internet
On-the-job training for a very specific task

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the specific tasks mentioned as a fine-tuning example?
What does fine-tuning change inside the model?
options: Its internal parameter dials, weights, and biases

questions.question: What is Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) based on?
options: Input/output pairs showing the AI a perfect answer

questions.question: In SFT, what kind of dataset is required?
If the AI is shown 1,000 examples of a specific MUN reminder tone during SFT, what is the likely outcome?
options: The model permanently adopts the new personality and style more strongly

questions.question: Which of these is the best example of an SFT output from the chapter?
options: A polished reminder with emojis and MUN details
A random sequence of token IDs

questions.question: What is the main limitation of SFT that RLHF is designed to improve?
options: SFT does not always guarantee helpful, safe, and non-harmful behavior

questions.question: RLHF is compared in the chapter to training a puppy using:
Which company/model transition is explicitly mentioned as an example of RLHF's impact?
What is the first step in the RLHF process described in the chapter?
In RLHF, what do human workers do after the AI generates several answers?
options: They rank the answers using a strict rubric
They delete the worst answer permanently

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to earn a high reward score in RLHF?
options: A polite, helpful, and accurate answer
A rude answer with false claims
An answer that ignores the prompt

questions.question: What kind of score does a rude or dangerous answer receive in RLHF according to the chapter?
What does RLHF ultimately teach the AI to do?
options: Chase the highest mathematical reward and align with human values
Use only one token per reply

questions.question: Which term best describes the AI output produced by a reward-based training process in RLHF?
Why is RLHF considered a reinforcement learning method?
options: Because the model learns by maximizing reward and minimizing penalty
Because it does not involve rankings

questions.question: What is the 'Black Box' problem in LLMs?
options: The model cannot process black text
The model's exact outputs are hard to predict because it generates new text from many parameter combinations
The model cannot use a tokenizer

questions.question: Why is observability needed after launching a chatbot?
options: To prevent the model from learning language
To monitor what the AI is actually saying and catch problems quickly

questions.question: What can prompt injection potentially do to an AI system?
options: Force it to swear or behave unexpectedly
Remove the need for a dashboard

questions.question: Which problem is specifically mentioned as something observability should catch?
LLM Observability is compared to a car's:
Which metric in observability tracks how long it takes for the first token to appear?
Why is Time to First Token especially important for Gen Z users according to the chapter?
options: If it takes too long, they may close the app
They do not care about speed

questions.question: What does token cost represent in LLM observability?
options: The number of human judges used
The money charged for tokens the AI reads and writes
The size of the tokenizer vocabulary

questions.question: Why do observability dashboards track exact token usage?
options: To prevent the system from becoming a CNN
To avoid accidentally spending too much money

questions.question: What is drift in the context of observability?
options: A model becoming slower due to the internet
Behavior changes over time that move the AI away from its original training
The ranking done by human workers

questions.question: Which of the following is the best purpose of observability in a production AI system?
options: To hide all logs from engineers
To track, record, and analyze conversations in real time
To eliminate the need for evaluation
To prevent users from asking questions

questions.question: What is the modern solution for grading human-like text called?
Why is LLM-as-a-Judge useful?
options: It grades answers using deep understanding instead of only strict word matching
It removes the need for rubrics

questions.question: In the MUN analogy, what represents the Judge LLM?
What information is sent to the Judge LLM in the observability pipeline?
options: The prompt, the chatbot's answer, and the rubric

questions.question: What might a grading rubric ask the Judge LLM to score?
options: Latency, GPU Temperature, and Costs only

questions.question: What does the Judge LLM typically return after evaluating an answer?
options: A grade and a brief explanation

questions.question: Which feature makes LLM-as-a-Judge more powerful than simple word matching?
options: It works only with exact string matches

questions.question: What is the first step in the continuous feedback loop described in the chapter?
In the feedback loop, what happens after the observability dashboard flags a bad conversation?
If the Judge LLM confirms that the chatbot failed the Accuracy test, what is the next logical step if the issue was rude tone?
options: Create a new dataset from the corrected conversation and run SFT
Change the model to a CNN

questions.question: Why is the continuous feedback loop considered the heartbeat of the modern AI industry?
options: Because it allows systems to get smarter every day
Because it removes all mistakes instantly
Because it eliminates the need for training

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the combined purpose of pipelines, vector databases, fine-tuning, and observability?
options: They are the exact skills used by top AI engineers in applied AI systems
They only matter for image generation
They are unrelated to real-world AI deployment

questions.question: In production, why is an AI system often compared to a black box?
options: Because its outputs can be hard to predict exactly
Because it cannot process any inputs
Because it only uses one token
Because it is made of metal

questions.question: What is the most likely danger of not having observability in a live chatbot?
options: You may not notice hallucinations, unsafe behavior, or prompt injection attacks
The hub will stop hosting models

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the flow from raw data to final answer in the chapter?
options: Extract → Transform → Load → Tokenize → Model → Decode

questions.question: Which part of the HuggingFace pipeline is most directly responsible for converting user text into numbers the model can understand?
Which component is most likely to be downloaded automatically from the HuggingFace Hub in a real inference pipeline?
options: A pre-trained model and its matching tokenizer

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why data must be transformed before loading?
options: Raw text is messy and the model needs numerical input
The GPU can only read emojis
The tokenizer cannot work on numbers
The model only understands broken links

questions.question: What is the most accurate description of a prompt in the chapter's pipeline view?
options: The user text that begins the inference process
The reward score given after training

questions.question: Why is inference described as the technical term for asking AI a question and getting an answer?
options: Because it refers to using a trained model to produce output
Because it means only training a tokenizer
Because it is the same as human ranking

questions.question: What is the strongest reason pre-trained models are compared to college graduates?
options: They possess broad general knowledge before specific job training
They are always perfect at one niche task
They do not need any more training
They can only answer yes/no questions

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes pre-training from fine-tuning?
options: Pre-training learns general language rules; fine-tuning adapts the model to a specific task
Pre-training is done only with human judges; fine-tuning is done only with tokenizers
Pre-training happens after deployment; fine-tuning happens before deployment
Pre-training removes weights; fine-tuning removes biases

questions.question: In the chapter, what is the main goal of pre-training an LLM?
options: To learn the next-word prediction task from internet-scale text
To create reward scores from humans
To track token cost in a dashboard

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the idea of supervised fine-tuning?
options: Showing the AI exact prompt-answer examples of ideal behavior
Letting the AI explore randomly without examples
Using only reward scores without labels
Training the AI on images only

questions.question: Why does the chapter say SFT can permanently adopt a new personality or style?
options: Because repeated high-quality examples slightly adjust the model's parameters
Because the tokenizer changes the font
Because the model forgets all general knowledge

questions.question: What role do human workers play in RLHF?
options: They rank model outputs using a safety and helpfulness rubric
They generate every final token manually
They remove the need for reinforcement learning

questions.question: Which of the following would most likely be rewarded in RLHF?
options: An answer that is polite, helpful, and accurate
An answer that is rude but very long
An answer that is unsafe but confident
An answer that ignores the user's request

questions.question: Which of the following is the best summary of the reward model in RLHF?
options: It learns to score answers based on human ranking preferences

questions.question: Why is RLHF especially useful for making AI safe?
options: It teaches the model to prefer helpful and safe responses over harmful ones
It deletes unsafe words from the dictionary automatically
It prevents the AI from answering questions

questions.question: What is the most direct connection between observability and fine-tuning in the feedback loop?
options: Observability identifies problems, and fine-tuning corrects them in the model
Observability replaces the model, and fine-tuning replaces the dashboard
Observability creates tokens, and fine-tuning creates latency
Observability prevents any need for evaluation

questions.question: Which issue would most likely be caught by the 'Drift' metric?
options: The AI begins acting strangely compared with its original training behavior
The AI's prompt is too short
The tokenizer has too many vowels
The model has no attention mask

questions.question: Which issue would most likely be caught by the token cost metric?
options: The chatbot suddenly begins using too many tokens and becomes expensive
The chatbot uses a wrong rubric
The model forgets how to decode

questions.question: Which issue would most likely be caught by latency monitoring?
options: The first token takes too long to appear

questions.question: What is the best explanation of the 'Judge LLM' role in evaluation?
options: It grades outputs from a smaller AI app based on context and rubric

questions.question: Why is a judge model more suitable than exact word matching for human-like text?
options: Because it can evaluate meaning, tone, accuracy, and safety
Because it can only count words

questions.question: What is the final objective of the continuous feedback loop?
options: To make the AI system smarter every day through monitoring and correction

questions.question: In the feedback loop, what kind of conversation is most valuable for future correction?
options: A corrected conversation where the AI made a mistake
A conversation with no issues and no analysis
A conversation that never reaches observability
A conversation that only contains token IDs

questions.question: Which sequence best describes the production AI improvement cycle from the chapter?
Which of the following is the most accurate description of applied AI systems?
options: AI systems built using models, pipelines, and tools to solve real tasks

questions.question: Which combination is most directly responsible for turning raw prompt text into a user-visible answer in the HuggingFace workflow?
Why are open-source models important in the Model Hub?
options: They let developers reuse powerful pre-trained AI models rather than starting from zero
They remove the need for training data

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the relationship between Transformers and HuggingFace?
options: Transformers are a key library that helps engineers connect models and datasets in code
Transformers are a replacement for all datasets
Transformers are only used in RLHF

questions.question: Which task is most directly handled by a tokenizer during inference?
options: Converting prompt text into model-readable integers and later decoding outputs back to text

questions.question: What does the chapter imply is the key to building safe and useful custom AI apps?
options: Combining pipelines, pre-trained models, fine-tuning, and observability correctly

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the progression taught in Module 3?
options: From using pre-trained models through pipelines, to fine-tuning behavior, to monitoring and improving systems in production
From images to sounds to robots only
From raw code to no code to zero models
From weights to filters to pooling only
